content:
Why Lenders, Buyers and Insurers Ask for an Engineer Letter

When a home inspection notes cracks, uneven floors, or past foundation repair, the next request is often for a structural engineer's letter. Lenders want to know the property is sound before they fund a loan. Buyers want to know whether they are inheriting a repair bill. Insurers and title companies may want documentation of past work. A letter signed and sealed by a licensed Professional Engineer (PE) answers those questions with a professional opinion based on what the engineer observed and measured.

The Most Common Types of Engineer Letters

1. Structural engineer letter for a lender

Some loan programs and underwriters require an engineer's statement when an appraisal or inspection flags a structural concern. The letter typically states the condition of the foundation or framing, whether the issue affects safety or habitability, and whether repairs are needed before closing.

2. Engineer letter for closing (buyer or seller)

Buyers use an engineer evaluation to decide whether to proceed, renegotiate, or request repairs. Sellers sometimes get one in advance so a buyer's inspection does not derail the sale. Either way, the letter documents the current condition and any recommendations.

3. Foundation clearance letter

A foundation clearance letter states that, at the time of inspection, the foundation is performing acceptably or that previous repairs were completed and the foundation is within acceptable limits. It is often requested when a home with past foundation work is sold.

4. Foundation repair verification (post-repair) letter

After a foundation repair company finishes, an independent engineer can inspect the work, take a floor elevation survey, and issue a letter verifying the repair was completed per the repair plan. This letter is often needed to transfer a repair warranty or to satisfy a future buyer.

What the Engineer Does

  1. Reviews any available reports: inspection report, prior repair documents, and warranties
  2. Walks the interior and exterior looking for cracks, separations, sticking doors and windows, and drainage issues
  3. Takes a floor elevation survey across the slab to measure how the foundation has moved
  4. Forms an opinion on whether the structure is performing acceptably and whether repairs are needed
  5. Issues a written, signed and sealed letter

What a Good Letter Includes

  • Property address, date of inspection, and the purpose of the letter
  • Description of the structure and foundation type
  • Observations and measurements, ideally with photos and an elevation plan
  • A clear conclusion: acceptable performance, or repairs recommended
  • For post-repair letters, confirmation of the work performed and the repair company's documents reviewed
  • The engineer's signature and PE seal, with the firm's state registration

Lenders and buyers look for a clear conclusion. A letter that only lists observations without an opinion often triggers more questions and delays the closing.

How Fast Can You Get One?

Closings run on deadlines, so speed matters. The site visit for a typical home takes one to two hours, and the sealed letter usually follows within a few business days. Book as soon as an inspection raises a structural question, and tell the engineer your closing date up front.

What Affects the Cost?

  • Size of the home and number of stories
  • Whether a floor elevation survey is needed
  • Whether the letter covers a past repair that must be reviewed
  • Rush turnaround to meet a closing date

faq.question: What is a structural engineer letter for a lender?
faq.answer: It is a PE-sealed statement on the structural condition of a property, usually requested when an appraisal or inspection flags a concern. It states whether the structure is sound and whether repairs are needed before the loan closes.

faq.question: What is a foundation clearance letter?
faq.answer: A letter from a licensed engineer stating that, at the time of inspection, the foundation is performing acceptably or that previous repairs were completed and the foundation is within acceptable limits.

faq.question: What is a foundation repair verification letter?
faq.answer: A post-repair letter in which an engineer inspects completed foundation repair work, often with a floor elevation survey, and confirms it was completed per the repair plan. It is often used to transfer a warranty or reassure a buyer.

faq.question: How fast can I get an engineer letter for closing?
faq.answer: The site visit typically takes one to two hours, and the sealed letter usually follows within a few business days. Tell the engineer your closing date when you book.

faq.question: Who pays for the engineer letter?
faq.answer: Usually whoever requests it, the buyer, seller, or owner, although parties sometimes negotiate the cost as part of the sale.
